\[
H = \prod_k H_k,\quad (u_k, v_k) = k\,(f_{x0}, f_{y0}),\ k = 1 \ldots 3,\quad f_{x0} = 0.125,\ f_{y0} = 0
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \((f_{x0}, f_{y0})\): The base frequency in cycles per pixel
- \((u_k, v_k)\): The center of harmonic k
- \(H_k\): The high-pass factor of the notch at harmonic k and its mirror points

The comb filter is a notch-reject filter whose notches sit at k times the base frequency, up to the chosen count. Harmonics whose fx or fy passes 0.5 cycles per pixel are left out. Each harmonic is notched at its mirror points too, as in the notch-reject filter. Gonzalez and Woods build notch filters from high-pass factors. Placing them on harmonics is this filter's own convenience.
